title: 48 Hours Alone in Lisbon (I Got So Lost)
creator: Jess Ahn
description:
My first solo trip in Europe! Two days in Lisbon: trams, pastel de nata, getting lost in Alfama, and the best sunset of my life.

Use code JESSGOES for 15% off your first Airalo eSIM: https://airalo.com

Music: Epidemic Sound
Instagram: @jessgoesplaces

sentences.t: Okay, it's seven a.m., I've been awake for like thirty hours, and I'm in Lisbon!
The plan for today is the twenty-eight tram, a pastel de nata, and then just wander around Alfama until my legs give out.
The tram is exactly as cute as everyone says, but also, it is packed, I have someone's backpack in my face right now.
Hi, sorry, that's not your fault.
Okay, we made it to the top, and look at this view, all the orange roofs going down to the river.
So here's where things went a little wrong.
Alfama is basically a maze, the streets curve, they split, half of them turn into staircases, and none of them go where you think.
I wandered for like two hours taking photos, which was amazing, until I realized I had no idea where I was.
And by the time I found a tram stop, my phone was at four percent and I had no idea where my hostel was.
Which, honestly, is exactly why the very first thing I do now when I land somewhere is sort out my data.
Because the problem that day wasn't really the battery, it was that I'd been too scared of roaming charges to use my maps at all.
So this video is sponsored by Airalo, which is an eSIM store, and it has completely changed how I travel.
You download the app, pick the country or region you're going to, and install a data plan before you even get on the plane.

If you want to try it, use code JESSGOES for fifteen percent off your first eSIM, and the link is in my description.
Okay so, back to me being lost at four percent.
I ended up asking an older lady outside a bakery, and she did not speak English, and I do not speak Portuguese.
But she walked me three streets over, pointed at a staircase, said something very firmly, and left.
And the staircase went straight down to my hostel!
I don't know who you are, but thank you, you're the real hero of this video.
After a nap that was supposed to be twenty minutes and was actually three hours, I went to get the famous custard tarts.
Okay, first bite.
Oh my gosh, it's still warm, the top is all caramelized, and the pastry just shatters.
I have cinnamon on my face, I don't care.
I ate two, and then I went back for a third one, and the guy at the counter definitely judged me.
For sunset everyone told me to go to one of the miradouros, which are these little viewpoints all over the city.
I picked one that was supposed to be less crowded, and it was not less crowded, but people were playing guitar and passing around little cups of cherry liqueur.
And honestly, watching the sun go down over the river with a bunch of strangers was the best part of the whole trip.
Tomorrow I'm taking the train out to Sintra to see the palaces, so make sure you're subscribed for that one.
Thanks for hanging out with me, and I'll see you in the next one.
